title: Protocol for Apoptosis Assay by Flow Cytometry Using Annexin V Staining Method
markdown:
## Protocol: Annexin V and propidium iodide flow-cytometric quantification of apoptosis in cultured cells

### Overview

This protocol outlines the procedure for quantifying apoptosis in cultured cells using Annexin V and propidium iodide (PI) via flow cytometry. The method involves seeding cells, incubating for 48 hours, harvesting both floating and adherent cells, staining with specific fluorochromes, and analyzing cell viability based on fluorescence profiles.

### Materials/Reagents

Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), Trypsin, Incubation buffer, Annexin V (1 mg/ml stock), Propidium iodide (1 mg/ml stock).

### Equipment

T25 culture flasks, Flow cytometer, Centrifuge, Pipettes, Tubes for cell collection.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain sterile technique during cell handling. Use appropriate personal protective equipment when handling chemicals such as trypsin and propidium iodide.

## Cell Culture and Harvest

### Day 0

1. Seed 1 x 10^6 cells into a T25 culture flask. Perform this step in triplicate for experimental groups. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare three additional T25 culture flasks for control groups: one for unstained controls, one for Annexin V only controls, and one for propidium iodide only controls. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->

### After 48 h incubation

1. After 48 hours of incubation, collect the supernatant containing floating apoptotic cells from each flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S01 -->
2. Trypsinize the adherent cells from each T25 flask to obtain approximately 2 x 10^6 cells per flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S02 -->
3. Combine the collected floating cells and the trypsinized adherent cells from respective flasks to create six distinct cell samples (tubes). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S03 -->

### Washing Phase

1. Wash the collected cell pellets twice with PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S01 -->
2. Centrifuge the washed cells at 670 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature (RT) after each wash. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S02 -->

### Staining Preparation

1. Re-suspend each resulting cell pellet (containing ~2 x 10^6 cells) in 400 μl of PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S01 -->

#### Branch A: Experimental Cells

1. For experimental cells (triplicates): Add 100 μl of incubation buffer containing 2 μl of Annexin V (1 mg/ml) and 2 μl of propidium iodide (1 mg/ml) to the 400 μl cell suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S02 -->

#### Branch B: Control Cells

1. For Control 1 (unstained): Mix 400 μl of cell suspension with 100 μl of incubation buffer without adding any stains. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S03 -->
2. For Control 2 (Annexin V only): Mix 400 μl of cell suspension with 100 μl of incubation buffer containing 2 μl of Annexin V (1 mg/ml). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S04 -->
3. For Control 3 (propidium iodide only): Mix 400 μl of cell suspension with 100 μl of incubation buffer containing 2 μl of propidium iodide (1 mg/ml). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T3-S05 -->

### Flow Cytometry Analysis

1. Analyze all stained and control samples immediately using flow cytometry without washing the cells prior to analysis. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T4-S01 -->
2. Interpret results as follows: Cells negative for both PI and Annexin V are healthy; cells negative for PI but positive for Annexin V are apoptotic; cells positive for both PI and Annexin V are necrotic. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T4-S02 -->
